update: {"kind": "procedure_update_v2", "procedure": "Maintain a compact ledger of live obligations. For each, retain origin authorization, target/operation, activation or continuation trigger, current order plus revision source, requested extent, status (waiting, ready, submitted, partial, complete, canceled), and latest receipt correlated to the exact action and extent. Carry authorization and triggers across intervening work; a continuation activates a retained waiting/partial item without repeating its origin. A partial receipt preserves only the uncompleted extent; submission is not completion. Apply revisions only to stated scope and preserve prior order needed for relative references. Remove an item only on explicit applicable cancellation or a receipt proving its requested extent complete. Keep conditional work authorized-but-waiting, distinguish authorization/readiness/completion, preserve unresolved conflicts as uncertain, and compact discharged history before dropping live fields or evidence IDs. Do not infer obligations from observations, capabilities or actor assumptions; record actual changes and evidence IDs in the native format. Record conditional future work as authorized but waiting for its stated condition, not unauthorized. Distinguish authorization from readiness and completion. Carry forward the originating authorization and continuation trigger across unrelated intervening work. A short continuation request need not repeat the original authorization. Remove an obligation only on an explicit applicable cancellation or a receipt proving its requested extent complete. One successful segment leaves the remainder pending when the request requires more. A submitted action is only a commitment until the correlated receipt. A revision changes only its stated scope; retain the original ordering needed to resolve relative references. Before saving, check each previously pending or conditional obligation: either retain it with its trigger, or cite the cancellation/completion event that discharges it. Never turn an actor assumption about authorization into a user restriction. Preserve unresolved conflicts as uncertain. Within the shared memory budget prioritize live obligations and evidence IDs over coordinates or verbose completed-job descriptions; compact discharged jobs. Do not invent a plan, task, restriction, dependency or completion. History records the actual change and its evidence."}
